name: Tryout
why: Borrows any shop card's On Recruit without paying, a clever link to every color, though it reads more like copying than recruiting.

name: Gather
why: Red's plain fuel space; the recruit bonus is a mild nudge nobody else at the table notices.

name: Walk-In
why: A free blind member is a real rush, and the +1 red to each rival keeps it from feeling one-sided.

name: Promote
why: Trading up into the leader's best card is the strongest catch-up swing on Red; the victim still gets a card back.

name: Demote
why: Mirror of Promote with a weaker pull; useful to dump a bad card, but a new player wonders why they'd take less.

name: Initiation
why: Free member up to 8 is a clear big round III moment; the choice is mostly which card, not whether.

name: Body Snatchers
why: A swap every round start gives Red a recurring threat that Loyalists and Deprogrammers play off; equal cost keeps it fair.

name: Volunteer
why: A 1-cost body: good fodder for the red count and Promote, but nobody notices it fire.

name: Mentor & Protégés
why: Two recruits in one and +3 to the red count feels big, but at 9 cost nobody can Promote or Demote it.

name: Proselytizers
why: Steady follower drip that rewards whoever already recruits most; nobody at the table reacts.

name: Mob
why: Big payoff for winning the red count, but pure leader-reward at 12 cost that rivals can't move.

name: Recruiter
why: 6 cost for +1 red per recruit is a small trigger that rarely pays back.

name: Patriarch
why: Generic member-count scorer that would work the same in any cult.

name: Greeters
why: Cheap body worth 2 that quietly feeds every color's On Recruit; invisible to rivals.

name: Deprogrammers
why: Turns every Red swap into a sting, but worth 4 for 3 cost reads as an always-buy.

name: Panel
why: Promoting or demoting your own member is hard to picture cold (with whom? the shop?).

name: Loyalists
why: A clean defense against Body Snatchers, but it's unclear whether Promote and Demote count as swaps.

name: Clerk
why: +1 red each round for 5 resources: forgettable and never the right buy.

name: Sleep In
why: Big purple for giving up tempo, and it plays with the Went Last contest and Night Watch.

name: Hold Up
why: A skip the victim can see coming and shrug off; 'even yours' adds a real timing choice.

name: Right Away
why: Clean double turn for grabbing two contested spaces; small resource gain.

name: Last Call
why: Strong payoff for holding minions and takes the token from rivals, but the two halves take a read.

name: Crunch Time
why: Three placements in a row is a big, plain rule bend that lets you lock a color's spaces.

name: Overtime
why: An extra minion in round III is plainly strong; few decisions around it.

name: Courier
why: A rainbow of resources for double turns links purple timing to Yellow sets and snake ends.

name: Night Watch
why: Pays only when a rival chooses the Goes Last token; the owner can't make it happen.

name: Night Owls
why: An extra minion each round from II, placed right away, which also chases the Went Last contest.

name: Early Birds
why: A cheap clean block on Hold Up and Bouncers; worth 2 for 3 makes it easy filler.

name: Bouncers
why: Two skipped rivals on recruit is a felt moment that combos with Gossip; what a skip means takes a read.

name: Gossip
why: Pays off every skip at the table, a nice hub for Hold Up and Bouncers.

name: Timekeeper
why: Generic per-color-member Game End scorer, same shape as several other colors.

name: Closer
why: A race for the last minion of the round, tied straight to Purple's contest.

name: Hot Streak
why: A big once-a-game payoff for building a chain, but counting the turns in a row is fiddly at the table.

name: Shift Crew
why: Vanilla 4 for 4 with nothing purple about it.

name: Night Shift
hardFail: needs tracking a table can't do (which minion was placed before which skip) and can't be read cold
why: Unreadable chain of conditions, and the table would have to remember skip order and minion ownership.

name: Toast
why: A big silver gain with a small gift to everyone; whether the gift counts for Caterer is unclear.

name: Polish
why: A clean 2-for-4 color fix that feeds Yellow sets; nobody else notices.

name: Party Gifts
why: Picking who gets the silver and feeding their silver count for followers is a real, social choice.

name: Potluck
why: Every rival picks what to give and gets paid back, so the whole table takes part.

name: Sweet Talk
why: Open-ended conversion; useful but plain and close to Polish.

name: Largesse
why: A huge gift for followers that hands rivals the silver contest: a real round III tension.

name: Godparent
why: Giving a member away for followers plays off Old Maid, Martyrs and Red's swaps.

name: Hostesses
why: A steady gift-for-followers each round that feeds Caterer and the silver contest.

name: Caterer
why: +1 silver per gift is small, and 'gifted' leaves Toast and Potluck unclear.

name: Toastmaster
why: +1 follower per Silver space: a small trigger nobody notices.

name: Debutantes
why: Doubling a hoard at the right moment is a big, timed swing in the silver contest.

name: Smooth Talkers
why: Strong flexibility, but 11 cost puts it out of reach of the swaps and favors whoever is already rich.

name: Philanthropist
why: A smaller Largesse on a card; repeats its sibling space.

name: Polisher
why: A once-a-game Polish; repeats the space.

name: Creditor
why: Aim it at the leader each round; they lose followers but gain silver, so it stings fairly and helps you catch up.

name: Debt Collectors
why: Pulls gifted silver back once to swing the silver contest; feels more like taking than giving.

name: High Society
why: Pays when rivals take Silver spaces; passive, but gives a reason to watch the color.

name: Envy
hardFail: relies on a rival having more resources (silver) than you
why: Pays only when a rival holds more silver than you, and it reads like it was pasted in from another color.

name: Harvest
why: Yellow's plain anchor; choosing colors gives it a little shape.

name: Leaders' Tax
why: Reads where rivals went and taxes the busy color: a neat board read.

name: New Blood
why: Rewards recruiting a new color, which steers the shop draft.

name: Big New Blood
why: A bigger New Blood; strong, but it repeats its sibling.

name: Melting Pot
why: Pays for having many colors; an engine payoff that nobody else feels.

name: Makeover
why: A full rearrange is a strong set-maker and contest fixer in round III.

name: Gardeners
why: Fills the colors you lack, so it helps the player furthest from full sets.

name: Customs Officer
why: A small consolation when you're robbed; 6 cost for +1 yellow is dead.

name: Tourist
why: Followers every round for color spread, an engine you can see coming.

name: Harmonist
why: A Game End payoff for full sets, the contest's own measure.

name: Dyer
why: The same shape as Tourist and Caravan with a weaker payoff.

name: Meddler
why: Changing everyone's resources can break their sets and contests; rivals feel it.

name: Drifters
why: A wild color slot that tips By-color counts and yellow sets; a real choice when you recruit it.

name: Big Tent
why: A scorer that pushes you toward one of everything, which shapes your recruits.

name: Caravan
why: A strong engine with no counter at 9 cost; another 'per color you hold' card.

name: Tastemaker
why: Few cards change rivals' resources, so it rarely fires.

name: Savings
why: Fuel plus a small shop bend that denies a rival their card.

name: Out of Style
why: Wiping a color off the shop is a visible table-wide move that hits rivals' plans.

name: Peek
why: Strong control of the pile, but hidden knowledge rivals can't follow.

name: Recruit Twice
why: A plain, strong extra buy that empties the shop.

name: Bury
why: Deny a card for half its cost in blue; the math is a small barrier.

name: Spree
why: Three buys is a clear round III climax.

name: Hawker
why: Each rival has a real pay-or-let-go choice; wordy, with recruiting out of turn.

name: Patroness
why: Blue buries constantly, so this becomes a quiet follower engine.

name: Snobs
why: Generic per-color-member Game End scorer.

name: Window Shopper
why: Sends rivals' targets away and pays in their colors.

name: Shopaholics
why: Double buys every turn is a runaway engine at 9 cost that nobody can move.

name: Window Dressers
why: Cheap 3 bodies for the blue count with a one-time shop churn.

name: Doormen
why: Forced swaps with the shop each round are strong but take a lot of words.

name: Regular
why: +1 blue on follower buys: forgettable and off theme.

name: Trendsetters
why: Each recruit also buries a card, a steady way to deny rivals.

name: Critic
why: +1 follower when rivals buy blue: small and passive.

name: Scavenger
why: Turns rivals' burying into your chance at the card: a sharp counter to Blue's own spaces.

name: Help Yourself
why: Aimed theft that splits as you choose, the color's core.

name: Stash
why: Magenta's plain anchor; the same shape as Gather and Allowance.

name: Lie Low
why: Small steal plus a shield: a block the table respects.

name: Heist
why: Straight follower theft aimed at the leader is a big catch-up swing.

name: Shake Down
why: The victim picks their own punishment, which feels bad.

name: Poach
why: Taking any rival's member in round III is a big, aimable moment.

name: Cutpurse
why: A steady drip off the biggest hoard; no aiming choice, but it checks hoards.

name: Accomplice
why: A cheap one-shot steal; plain.

name: Grifter
why: Scales with your cult size, so it rewards the leader.

name: Second-Story Man
why: A steal right before contests, timed to flip a contest: tense and readable.

name: Desperado
why: Turns being behind into bigger steals: real catch-up.

name: Extortionist
why: A bigger Cutpurse; repeats its sibling.

name: Bodyguards
why: The clean answer to theft; a defensive buy with no payoff of its own.

name: Double Agent
why: A swap through itself; strange to read and feels more Red than Magenta.

name: Kidnapper
why: Taking a member from the same rival every round before round III feels like being robbed.

name: Shoplifter
why: A small steal with each recruit; fine filler.

name: Fence
why: A deterrent that makes thieves think twice.

name: Allowance
why: White's plain anchor; a near twin of Stash and Gather.

name: Splurge
why: Rewards an expensive recruit; 'every 1 in round II' leaves round III unclear.

name: Exchange
why: A small resource-to-followers conversion; plain.

name: Farewell
why: Cashing out a member for its cost combos with Martyrs and the Fewest-followers contest.

name: Estate Sale
why: A weaker twin of Farewell.

name: Cash In
why: A clean round III cash-out that pays for holding white.

name: Recluse
why: Pays the small cult, a real counter-plan to member-heavy rivals.

name: Landlord
why: Plain steady income.

name: Heiresses
why: 9 cost for one burst of white; rarely worth it.

name: Brokers
why: A cheap 3 that boosts White's own follower spaces; 'White action' takes a read.

name: Misers
why: Holding white against cashing it in is a real tension.

name: Raiders
why: A once-a-game follower steal with a small payment; strong catch-up.

name: Cashier
why: Cash In on a card, with real timing; repeats the space.

name: Money Changers
why: Gets paid whenever anyone buys followers; a cheap 2.

name: Martyrs
why: Punishes takers and pays off Farewell and Godparent: a great connector.

name: Old Money
why: Generic per-color-member Game End scorer.

name: Hoarder
why: Sets up Cash In and Misers in one move, with real timing.

name: Build Up
why: Green's plain anchor.

name: Echo
why: Copies whatever the last player did, so every turn becomes a read of the table.

name: Reprise
why: Repeat your best space; a solid engine piece.

name: Sample
why: Borrow a rival's On Recruit; it reads their cult.

name: Cover
why: Lets you use a space nobody has taken; a neat flex.

name: Greatest Hits
why: A big round III payoff for a cult full of On Recruits that rewards the leader.

name: Busker
why: Plain steady green income.

name: Impersonator
why: Steals a rival's ability each round; strong, but the table has to remember which.

name: Impressionist
why: Small rebates on every copy at the table.

name: Wallflower
why: Doubling copies is a big engine for the copier who's already ahead.

name: Fan Club
why: Copy the leader's space, a clever catch-up that reads the table.

name: Roadie
why: Income that scales with green members.

name: Stunt Double
why: Recruit it right after a big space to do it twice: clear timing.

name: Tribute Band
why: Doing a rival's whole round is a dramatic swing, but 14 cost puts it out of reach of any answer.

name: Doppelganger
why: Copying your best member is strong; whether its On Recruit fires again is unclear.

name: Agents
why: A clean block against copying.

name: Chronicler
why: Generic per-color-member Game End scorer.

name: Party Crasher
why: Bending the one-per-space rule once is a big, aimable moment.

name: Alchemists
why: Wild recruiting money worth 3 for 5 makes it close to a must-buy.

name: Extra Hand
why: 9 cost for one minion, once; rarely worth it.

name: Line Cutters
why: Cancels the fewest-followers-first catch-up, and worth 3 for 2 cost.

name: Old Maid
why: A poison card to hand rivals through Godparent and the swaps.

name: Dabblers
why: Wild count filler for the By-color contests; which counts it joins takes a read.

name: Anarchist
why: A swap of any two members every round; powerful but a lot to track.

name: Spoilsport
why: Cancelling a leader's contest is a felt sting that slows a runaway.

name: Con Men
why: A big one-shot steal; plain.

name: Sore Loser
why: Punishes the contest leader when you win none; ties are unclear.
